summary: An announcement from BBN with two items of network news. The first and main one is that the new IMP software, described in RFCs 331, 343 and 359, was released on July 18, 1972 and ran with few problems. BBN asks users to be patient and to report bugs.

eli5.summary: After many tries, the new software for the network's traffic machines finally worked. The team is happy and asks people to tell them if anything seems off.

questions: how long did the new imp software run
subtitle: An announcement of the new IMP software release and network power failures.

tldr.problem: The ARPANET IMP software was being replaced with a new version, and power failures were disrupting network connectivity.
tldr.mechanism: BBN released new IMP software on July 18, 1972 and asked the network community to report any issues. Regarding power, the memo documented recent failures and encouraged patience.
tldr.outcome: The new IMP system ran successfully with few problems, though a TIP allocation issue and summer power constraints remained.

today: RFC 374 is Unknown status. It is a historical record of the ARPANET's transition to new IMP software in summer 1972.

sections.title: New IMP Software Released
sections.content: On Tuesday, July 18, 1972, the ARPANET released new IMP software described in earlier RFCs (331, 343, 359). The system ran from 10 AM that day through Wednesday afternoon with very few network problems. BBN was pleased with this performance and intended to keep the new system up permanently.
sections.eli5: After years of work, the new traffic-switching software finally went live and stayed up. The team was happy.

sections.title: Known Issues and Support
sections.content: BBN acknowledged that bugs might appear in a system of that size and asked the network community to report them. They also noted the new system might feel different to both terminal users and host computers. The main known issue was the TIP software problem where allocation control messages were sometimes missing, blocking the server-to-user path. This problem seemed most likely when multiple users were connected and the server host ran TENEX.
sections.eli5: New software always has bugs. The team asked people to tell them when something feels wrong. One problem: sometimes the new software lost track of resource deals, blocking connections.

sections.title: Site Power Problems
sections.content: During June 1972, between one-quarter and one-half of IMP downtime was due to site power failures. On July 15-16, two sites went down all weekend from air conditioning failure, leaving nine sites disconnected from the rest of the network through only one path, which then failed. On July 18, an underground power transformer at site 27 failed, taking IMP 27 offline for several hours.
sections.eli5: Summer heat was overloading power supplies. Some computers had to shut down, and two went dark for a whole weekend. The team asked everyone to be patient because they could not fix weather.
